children: Culp reported first quarter fiscal 2027 results with consolidated net sales of $54.0 million, up 6.5% year-over-year, and net income of $6.0 million, or $0.47 per diluted share. Consolidated gross profit was $15.4 million (28.5% of sales) which includes $6.9 million of tariff refunds; adjusted gross profit excluding tariff recoveries was $8.4 million (15.6% of sales). The company reduced net debt by over 70% to $3.1 million and generated $8.1 million of cash from operations in the quarter.
Revenue: Consolidated net sales of $53.973 million for the three months ended August 2, 2026, up 6.5% from $50.691 million a year earlier.
Gross profit: Reported consolidated gross profit of $15.378 million (28.5% of sales); adjusted gross profit excluding $6.940 million tariff refunds was $8.438 million (15.6% of sales).
Operating income: Reported operating income of $6.669 million (12.4% of sales); adjusted operating loss excluding tariff recoveries was $(0.271) million.
Net income and EPS: Net income of $5.981 million, or $0.47 per diluted share, versus a net loss of $(0.231) million in the prior-year quarter.

Liquidity and leverage: Net debt reduced to $3.089 million (cash and cash equivalents $10.235 million; total debt $13.324 million); cash from operations was $8.102 million and adjusted free cash flow was $8.028 million.

Bedding segment momentum: Bedding sales grew 13.2% year-over-year to $31.750 million despite one fewer selling week; adjusted bedding gross profit (excluding tariff recoveries) improved to $4.308 million, or 13.6% of segment sales.

Upholstery performance: Upholstery sales were $22.223 million, roughly flat year-over-year despite the shorter selling period; adjusted upholstery gross profit was $4.130 million, or 18.6% of segment sales, reflecting consistent operating margins.

Operational improvements: Management attributes improved margins and profitability to integration, restructuring and platform optimization efforts, enhanced U.S. operations, and flexible nearshore/offshore sourcing.

Balance sheet and cash management: Inventory reduction initiatives and tariff proceeds contributed to significant net-debt reduction and strengthened liquidity (total liquidity reported at $29.4 million at quarter end).

Outlook posture: Company expects modest sequential sales growth in Q2, aims for break-even operating income and accelerating adjusted EBITDA while prioritizing continued debt reduction and strategic use of China credit facilities.
